race_name: L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France

top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France. Practice on rolling fjord roads and three short climbs: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 79 miles.
65ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
79 miles on rolling fjord roads and three short climbs burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France. Train it until it feels boring.
At L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
5,151ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,151ft of climbing on rolling fjord roads and three short climbs does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on rolling fjord roads and three short climbs can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
5,151ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France's 79 miles. Start early, use products you tolerate, and carry enough between the organizer’s confirmed resupply points.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at L'Étape Trondheim by Tour de France rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on rolling fjord roads and three short climbs to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 79 miles of rolling fjord roads and three short climbs in Trondheim, Trøndelag, Norway.
